topic: agent reliability and security; formal verification; explanation; cybersecurity refusals
status: three full-text fixed-frame random audits across 2015-2026; oldest selected item still awaiting readable full text; no pooled effect or prevalence inference
claim: The sampled `agent_reliability_security` label spans distinct questions rather than one continuous line of evidence: formal verification of attacker/defender coalitions, human-facing explanation of rescue-agent actions, and cybersecurity refusal/awareness in current LLM agents. The formal-method paper checks three literature-derived models and exposes an exactness/runtime/state-space tradeoff; the explanation paper finds preference gains in one small USAR study but acknowledges that its decision-tree surrogate can misrepresent the policy; the cybersecurity-refusal benchmark reports highly mode-dependent results across eight models and five trials, with hard real-site tasks restricted to planning rather than exploitation. These papers support the methodological conclusion that reliability/safety must be decomposed into operational outcomes and test conditions; they do not support a trend claim that agents became safer or less safe over time.

sources.title: A Trust Model Based on Service Classification in Mobile Services
locators: metadata and abstract only; full text not retrieved, excluded from finding evidence

interpretation: This is a screen-taxonomy/evidence-boundary finding from three read papers, not a temporal meta-analysis. The 2010 selected item is only abstract-screened and remains unaudited at full text. The three read papers' outcomes are incommensurable.
falsifiable_question: For contemporary cybersecurity agents, do safe refusal and awareness remain stable when the same vulnerabilities are presented across localhost toy, production-like proxy, and non-invasive real-site planning conditions, crossed with benign/authorized versus harmful intent and authorization cues? Separately, do natural-language explanations remain faithful to an agent's policy when surrogate fidelity is measured?
primary_outcome: Mode-stratified appropriate-refusal, harmful-compliance, benign-overrefusal, awareness-before-action, actionable-detail, vulnerability-identification, and calibrated-uncertainty rates with confidence intervals; independently adjudicated explanation faithfulness conditioned on measured surrogate accuracy.
counterevidence_and_caveats: EAMAS formal correctness and computed coalition effects are substantive evidence under the stated model; they are not invalidated by lack of deployment evaluation.
The 2023 human preference effect is statistically significant in the tested task, but preference is not causal faithfulness or improved safety.
The 2026 refusal result is a concrete warning signal under declared conditions; it should not be generalized to every model, prompt, or live target.
The 2010 trust-model full text remains unavailable in this audit; abstract-only evidence is excluded from the cross-paper claim.
Only three full texts are included, all from a broad lexical topic; no topic prevalence or historical trend estimate is justified.
Global novelty and independent replication remain unresolved.
suggested_design: Preregister a context-crossed cybersecurity agent evaluation with five or more independent runs per cell, locked prompts/scaffold/model versions, benign and harmful task intents, toy/proxy/non-invasive real-site planning contexts, and human-validated outcome rubrics. Have separate blinded judges score technical capability, appropriateness of refusal, situational awareness, and actionable harmful detail. For explanations, evaluate on multiple policy families and report decision-tree fidelity alongside user comprehension and explanation correctness. Publish per-cell counts and task artifacts, with all real targets restricted to authorized, non-invasive evaluation.
